Roasted Butternut Squash Halves

Jump to RecipeStep By Step

By Aysegul Sanford

Published Oct 19, 2026

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 7:10
Instaread

These roasted butternut squash halves come out fork-tender with caramelized edges, and all it takes is trimming the stem and one lengthwise cut in the middle. I roast them cut-side up at 375°F, low and slow, so the flesh cooks all the way through.

I keep it simple with four basic ingredients, but you can add your favorite seasoning depending on how you want to use them. Serve them as-is for an easy fall side dish, or scoop out the flesh for other recipes.

Yields1 Butternut Squash
Prep Time5 minutes mins
Cook Time55 minutes mins
Total Time1 hour hr

Ingredient Notes and Seasoning Ideas

You will find the full list of ingredients with exact measurements in the recipe card below. 

The only ingredient worth a note is the squash itself. I use one large butternut squash, about 3 pounds. When you shop, look for one with a long, even neck and no bruises or blemishes.

For basic seasoning, my rule of thumb is to use 1 tablespoon olive oil, ½ teaspoon kosher salt, and ¼ teaspoon black pepper for every 3 pounds of butternut squash. 

If yours is smaller or larger, use less or more.

That said, if you want to get a bit more creative, below are a few of my favorite seasoning ideas:

  • Fresh Herbs: Sage, rosemary, or thyme. Start by sprinkling ½ teaspoon of chopped herbs over the oiled halves, along with salt and pepper, and add more if you like.
  • Spices: Ground cumin, ground coriander, chili powder, or even a pinch of cayenne pepper would work. Use one spice or mix and match as you like. Start by sprinkling ¼ teaspoon of each spice over the oiled halves and adjust from there.
  • Sweeteners: I recommend maple syrup or brown sugar. Start with 1 tablespoon, sprinkling the brown sugar or drizzling the maple syrup over the oiled halves.

How To Bake Butternut Squash Halves In The Oven

I often hear from readers that they dread cutting the squash most. I get it; for a long time, I felt the same way. So I started by showing you how to cut it. The information below should help, but for more detail, check out my guide on How to Cut Butternut Squash. 

If cutting feels too daunting, try my Whole Roasted Butternut Squash recipe.

Once the squash is cut, the rest is truly easy. 

Step 1 – Trim the top: Place the butternut squash on its side on a sturdy cutting board. Hold it firmly in the middle with your non-dominant hand. Using a sharp chef’s knife, trim the stem by cutting about ½ inch (1.3 cm) off. 

I skip the bottom, but you can trim it the same way.

If your butternut squash feels too hard to cut, you can soften it in the microwave first. Pierce the squash 6 to 8 times with a knife or fork, then microwave it on high for 2 minutes.

If it is still too firm, keep microwaving it in 30-second intervals until it softens enough to cut.

Step 2 – Cut it in half: While still holding it firmly on its side, cut it lengthwise down the middle, from top to bottom. I recommend making the cut in two passes: cut one side first, then turn it around and cut the other side.

You may need to gently rock the knife back and forth while applying a little pressure to loosen the squash as you cut. Do not rush this step. Go slow and steady.

Scoop out the seeds with a large spoon or an ice cream scoop, and discard them.

Step 3 – Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C). No need to line a sheet pan with parchment paper. Since the squash halves roast cut-side up, only the skin touches the pan, so nothing sticks.

Short on oven space? If you are making this for a holiday meal and your oven is in high demand, try my Air Fryer Butternut Squash Halves instead.

Step 4 – Arrange and season: Place the butternut squash halves, cut-side up, on a large baking sheet so the surface roasts and turns golden.

Cut side up or down? I tested both ways, and both work, but I chose cut side up because it puts the oiled, seasoned side toward the heat, which helps the natural sugars caramelize better.

Lightly brush the halves with 1 tablespoon olive oil, or spread it with your hands until evenly coated. Sprinkle with ½ teaspoon kosher salt and ¼ teaspoon ground black pepper.

If you are adding the optional seasonings:

  • Herbs and spices: Sprinkle them on with salt and pepper.
  • Maple syrup or brown sugar: Drizzle or sprinkle on in the last 10 minutes of roasting.

Step 5 – Bake the butternut squash: Roast for 50 to 55 minutes, or until the tops turn golden brown and the squash is fork-tender. 

Check doneness by inserting a knife into “the neck” of one butternut squash half, the thickest part. If it comes in and out easily, it is ready.

How long to roast butternut squash halves depends on their size. The squash in the photos weighs about 3 lb and took 50 to 55 minutes to cook. If yours is smaller, start checking after 45 minutes. If it is larger, it may take longer, so keep roasting and check every 5 minutes until the knife slides in easily.

Step 6 – Cool and serve: Let the butternut squash halves cool for about 5 to 10 minutes before serving or scooping out the flesh.

What To Do With Roasted Butternut Squash Halves

My favorite way to serve them is as-is for a simple side dish. Top them with a few tablespoons of butter while still hot, let it melt, and season with a little more salt and pepper.

You can also scoop out the flesh and mash it, or use it in my Butternut Squash Soup recipe, or cut it into cubes and add to my Butternut Squash and Quinoa Salad.

Roasted Butternut Squash Halves (Savory)

No ratings yet
By: Aysegul Sanford
Yields1 Butternut Squash
Prep Time5 minutes mins
Cook Time55 minutes mins
Total Time1 hour hr
Remove Ads
Roasted butternut squash halves with olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast cut-side up at 375°F until fork-tender with golden edges. Serve them as an easy fall side dish, or scoop out the flesh for other recipes.

Ingredients 

  • 1 butternut squash, 3 lbs
  • 1 tablespoon of olive oil
  • ½ teaspoon kosher salt
  • ¼ teaspoon black pepper

Instructions 

  • Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C). There is no need to line the sheet pan with parchment paper.
  • Place the whole butternut squash on its side on your cutting board. Hold it firmly in the middle with your non-dominant hand. Trim the stem (the top) by cutting about ½-inch off.
  • While still holding it firmly on its side, cut it vertically (or from top to bottom direction) in the middle. I recommend cutting one side first and then turning it around and cutting the other side next. As you are cutting you may have to jerk it back and forth while applying a little pressure to loosen it. Remove the seeds with a spoon and discard them.
  • Place the halved butternut squash cut side up on a baking sheet. Brush the cut side with olive oil and sprinkle it with salt and pepper.
  • Roast in the oven for about 50-55 minutes or until it turns golden brown. The timing might be a bit more or less depending on the size of your butternut squash. You can also check doneness by inserting a knife in "the neck" (the narrow upper part) of the squash. If it comes in and out easily it should be ready to go.
  • Let it cool for 5 minutes, use it in your recipe right away or scoop the flesh to use it later.

Notes

Make-ahead and storage: You can roast butternut squash halves up to 3 days before you plan to use them. 
To store, let them cool to room temperature, then wrap them in plastic wrap (or store them in an airtight container) and refrigerate for up to 3 days.
To reheat, place them on a sheet pan, cut-side up, and warm in a preheated 350°F oven for 10 to 15 minutes, until thoroughly heated through.
